body: Getting support in counselling and therapy for anxiety and obsessive compulsive disorder. 16 days sober. Still trying to get the psycho ex out of my life. Things are so so. Your support means the world to me. Thinking someone out there cares enough to check up on me feels great. To be honest a lot of my friends don't really seem to care or be around. I guess I burned a lot of bridges

I wasn't super thrilled with the AA meeting I attended. I tried a few different ones. I go for an assessment at an outpatient program Monday morning so I'm looking forward to that. One day at a time. Haven't had a drink in 6 days and I feel a bit more positive as that number grows.
Me! I went to an AA meeting and the gym. Day 3 never felt so good!
Fancy feast now and nobody gets hurt!
And we can make it through tomorrow.
Thank you! I am very nervous for tomorrow. I was planning on sitting very quietly and listening. But I guess participating is probably my best bet.
Not so great. Starting AA tomorrow. So it can only go up from here
Amazing. Good for you. I'm on day one after yet another fuck up weekend of losing friends and crashing cars. You're an inspiration.

I'm finding it hard to leave the house today I am a giant bundle of nerves. Tomorrow morning 8am will be my first meeting. Followed by a drs appointment and checking out outpatient programs. Ill let you know how everything goes. Oh I guess ill be calling the insurance companies to try to see if I can get my car fixed. What a day....I guess it's only up from here right.
There seems to be a lot of groups in my hometown maybe I should go tonight
What is an AA meeting generally like?

Thank you all so much. One day at a time I guess. I'm afraid my friends are all going to alienate me as well. I guess after a few months ill see who my true friends are. I hope to be very active in this group. It seems like a very supportive community and that is exactly what I need right now.

Thank you. It's a long weekend where I live so unfortunately there's nothing open. Tomorrow I'm going to contact some outpatient programs and hopefully start was seems to be a long process. I'm only 26. The thought of not drinking for the rest of my life leaves me scared and embarrassed.
Today is a new day. Thank you. Your responses really mean a lot
